362843.title: Nguyen–Stancu–Wei fundamental gap conjecture for horoconvex hyperbolic domains
362843.statement:
Let $N$ be the dimension, let $
\mathbb H^N$ be hyperbolic $N$-space, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb H^N$ be a horoconvex domain. Write $\Gamma(\Omega)$ for its fundamental gap, namely the difference between the first two Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian on $\Omega$. For a prescribed diameter bound $D>0$, **Nguyen–Stancu–Wei's conjecture.** There exists a constant $c(N,D)>0$ such that every horoconvex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb H^N$ of diameter at most $D$ satisfies

$$
\Gamma(\Omega)\geq c(N,D).
$$

The conjecture asserts a uniform positive lower bound for the fundamental gap under horoconvexity, in contrast with the arbitrarily small gaps possible for merely convex hyperbolic domains. The supplied source does not indicate whether this conjecture has been resolved.
362843.source_name: Gabriel Khan and Malik Tuerkoen, “Spectral Gap Estimates on Conformally Flat Manifolds”, arXiv:2404.15645 (2024).
362843.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15645

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362874.title: The inverse-polynomial Cheeger conjecture for zonotopes
362874.statement:
Let $Z$ be a zonotope of the form

$$
Z=\sum_{i=1}^k[-\bm{v_i},\bm{v_i}],
$$

and let $G$ be its $1$-skeleton. Let $i(G)$ denote the Cheeger constant, or edge-expansion, of $G$. **Inverse-polynomial Cheeger conjecture for zonotopes.** The quantity $i(G)$ is at worst inverse polynomial in $k$; equivalently, there is a polynomial $p$ such that $i(G)\geqslant 1/p(k)$. The conjecture would provide the weak isoperimetric control needed for percolation and connectivity arguments on zonotopes. The source calls it a bold conjecture and gives no proof or resolution.
362874.source_name: Maurício Collares, Joseph Doolittle and Joshua Erde, “The evolution of the permutahedron”, arXiv:2404.17260 (2026).
362874.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17260

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

363022.title: Aliniaeifard, van Willigenburg and Wang's spider e-positivity conjecture
363022.statement: For a partition $ambda=ambda_1\dotsmambda_d$ of $n-1$ with $d\ge 3$, the **spider** $S(\lambda)$ is the $n$-vertex tree consisting of paths of lengths $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d$ with a common end. A graph is **$e$-positive** when its chromatic symmetric function has nonnegative coefficients in the elementary symmetric-function basis. **Aliniaeifard, van Willigenburg and Wang's conjecture.** For any integer $m\ge 1$, the spider $S(4m+2,\,2m,\,1)$ is $e$-positive. The source attributes this conjecture to Aliniaeifard, van Willigenburg and Wang and gives no resolution.
363022.source_name: Davion Q. B. Tang, David G. L. Wang and Monica M. Y. Wang, “The spiders S(4m+2,\,2m,\,1) are e-positive”, arXiv:2405.04915 (2025).
363022.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04915

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2024). “Which graphs are $e$-positive? He also conjectured that all incomparability graphs of $(3+1)$-free posets are $e$-positive, which was confirmed by .”

363023.title: Aliniaeifard, van Willigenburg and Wang's generalized spider e-positivity conjecture
363023.statement: For positive integers $m,n$, let $S(a,b,c)$ denote the spider formed from three paths of lengths $a,b,c$ with a common end. A graph is **$e$-positive** when its chromatic symmetric function has nonnegative coefficients in the elementary symmetric-function basis. **Aliniaeifard, van Willigenburg and Wang's generalized conjecture.** For any integers $m,n\ge 1$, the spider $S(n(n!m+1),\,n!m,\,1)$ is $e$-positive. The source presents this as a further conjecture and gives no resolution.
363023.source_name: Davion Q. B. Tang, David G. L. Wang and Monica M. Y. Wang, “The spiders S(4m+2,\,2m,\,1) are e-positive”, arXiv:2405.04915 (2025).
363023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04915

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2024). “Which graphs are $e$-positive? He also conjectured that all incomparability graphs of $(3+1)$-free posets are $e$-positive, which was confirmed by .”

363027.title: The odd balanced complete bipartite graph conjecture for Trail Trap
363027.statement: Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with equal parts of size $n$, and let ${\rm P}{2}$ denote the second player in Trail Trap. A graph is ${\rm P}{2}$-win if the second player has a winning strategy. **Odd balanced complete bipartite graph conjecture.** For odd $n\geq 3$, $K_{n,n}$ is ${\rm P}{2}$-win. The cases $K_{3,3}$, $K_{5,5}$, and $K_{7,7}$ are known; the general claim remains open.
363027.source_name: Calum Buchanan, MacKenzie Carr, Alexander Clifton, Stephen G. Hartke, Vesna Iršič, Nicholas Sieger and Rebecca Whitman, “Trail Trap: a variant of Partizan Edge Geography”, arXiv:2405.05195 (2025).
363027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363143.title: Upward-flag conjecture for linear subdiagrams of spherical Artin diagrams
363143.statement: Let $A_S$ be an irreducible spherical Artin group with Dynkin diagram $\Lambda$. Let $\Lambda'$ be a linear subdiagram with consecutive vertices $\{s_i\}_{i=1}^n$, and assume that the edge between $s_{n-1}$ and $s_n$ has label at least $4$. Equip the vertex set of $\Delta_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}$ with the relation induced by $s_1<s_2<\cdots<s_n$. **Upward-flag conjecture.** This relation makes the vertex set a bowtie-free and upward-flag poset. The bowtie-free part is known in the source; the remaining upward-flag case is open in the stated generality.
363143.source_name: Jingyin Huang, “Cycles in spherical Deligne complexes and application to K(π,1)-conjecture for Artin groups”, arXiv:2405.12068 (2025).
363143.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12068

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363144.title: Downward-flag conjecture for $D_n$ subdivisions of relative Artin complexes
363144.statement: Let $A_S$ be an irreducible spherical Artin group. Let $S'\subset S$ be such that $A_{S'}$ has Dynkin diagram isomorphic to type $D_n$ for $n\geq 3$, without requiring the isomorphism to preserve edge labels. Let $\{b_i\}_{i=1}^{n+1}$ be the vertices specified in the source's Figure~ left, and form the $(b_1,b_2)$-subdivision of $\Delta_{S,S'}$. **$D_n$ subdivision conjecture.** This subdivision is a bowtie-free and downward-flag poset. The bowtie-free assertion and several special cases of the downward-flag assertion are known, but the remaining cases are open.
363144.source_name: Jingyin Huang, “Cycles in spherical Deligne complexes and application to K(π,1)-conjecture for Artin groups”, arXiv:2405.12068 (2025).
363144.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12068

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363244.title: Grünbaum's torus conjecture for cubic graph colorings
363244.statement: Let $G$ be a $2$-connected cubic graph embedded in the torus. The graph $G$ is **3-edge-colorable** if its edges can be colored with three colors so that adjacent edges receive different colors. **Grünbaum's torus conjecture.** If $G$ is not 3-edge-colorable, then $G$ contains two edges whose removal gives a planar graph. Grünbaum's broader conjecture for cubic graphs with polyhedral embeddings in orientable surfaces was disproved in genus $5$ by Kochol. The torus case remains unresolved; the conjecture is motivated by examples of toroidal snarks obtained from Petersen-graph constructions.
363244.source_name: Yuta Inoue, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Atsuyuki Miyashita, Bojan Mohar and Tomohiro Sonobe, “Three-edge-coloring projective planar cubic graphs: A generalization of the Four Color Theorem”, arXiv:2405.16586 (2024).
363244.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16586

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363419.title: Conjecture characterizing spanning sets in \mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_{2k}
363419.statement: Let $k$ and $s$ be positive integers. An **$s$-spanning set** of size $2$ in a finite abelian group is a two-element set whose signed sums of at most $s$ terms cover the group. **The $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_{2k}$ spanning-set conjecture.** The group $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_{2k}$ has an $s$-spanning set of size $2$ if and only if one of the following holds: $s$ is odd and $k\leq (s^2-1)/2$; $s$ is even and $k\leq (s^2-s)/2$; $s\equiv0\pmod 4$, $k$ is even, and $(s^2-s)/2<k\leq s^2/2$; or $s\equiv2\pmod 4$, $k\equiv2\pmod 4$, and $(s^2-s)/2<k\leq s^2/2$. The preceding exact results establish part of this classification, but the full characterization remains open.
363419.source_name: Bela Bajnok and W. Kyle Beatty, “On the Diameter of Undirected Cayley Graphs of Finite Abelian Groups”, arXiv:2406.04045 (2024).
363419.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04045

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363437.title: Akbari–Dalirrooyfard–Ehsani–Ozeki–Sherkati conjecture on forbidden out-degrees
363437.statement: Let $G$ be a loopless $d$-regular graph, with parallel edges permitted, and let $F\subseteq\{0,1,\ldots,d\}$ be a list of forbidden out-degrees. An orientation is **$F$-avoiding** if no vertex has out-degree in $F$. **Akbari–Dalirrooyfard–Ehsani–Ozeki–Sherkati conjecture.** If $|F|<\tfrac{1}{2}d$, then $G$ admits an $F$-avoiding orientation. The bound is tight if true: $K_{2k+1}$ has no $F$-avoiding orientation for $F=\{k,\ldots,2k-1\}$. The conjecture is known for bipartite graphs, cliques, and regular graphs of degree at most $4$, while the general case remains open; the source proves it for $d=5,6$.
363437.source_name: Owen Henderschedt and Jessica McDonald, “On orientations with forbidden out-degrees”, arXiv:2406.05095 (2024).
363437.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05095

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363497.title: Edoukou's conjecture on intersections with Hermitian threefolds
363497.statement:
Let $V_3$ be a non-degenerate Hermitian threefold in $\mathbb P^4(\mathbb F_{q^2})$, and let $F\in\mathbb F_{q^2}[x_0,\dots,x_4]$ be homogeneous of degree $d$. **Edoukou's conjecture.** If $d\leq q$, then

$$
|V(F)(\mathbb F_{q^2})\cap V_3|\leq d(q^5+q^2)+q^3+1.
$$

Moreover, this bound is attained by a threefold $V(F)$ in $\mathbb P^4$ if and only if $V(F)$ is a union of $d$ non-tangent hyperplanes $\Sigma_1,\dots,\Sigma_d$ defined over $\mathbb F_{q^2}$, such that the hyperplanes contain a common plane $\Pi$ defined over $\mathbb F_{q^2}$ and $\Pi$ intersects $V_3$ in a non-degenerate plane Hermitian curve. Edoukou proved the case $d=2$; the conjecture concerns the general range $d\leq q$ and the stated equality characterization.
363497.source_name: Mrinmoy Datta and Subrata Manna, “Maximum number of points on an intersection of a cubic threefold and a non-degenerate Hermitian threefold”, arXiv:2406.07326 (2024).
363497.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07326

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2024).

363540.title: Petruševski–Škrekovski edge-deletion conjecture for odd edge-colorings
363540.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph that is not a Shannon triangle of type $(2,2,2)$ or type $(2,2,1)$. Write $\chi_{\text{odd}}'(G)$ for the odd chromatic index, and call an edge **special** if its removal makes the graph odd $3$-edge-colorable. **Petruševski–Škrekovski edge-deletion conjecture.** Either

$$
\chi_{\text{odd}}'(G)\leq 3,
$$

or there exists a special edge $e$ whose removal makes the graph odd $3$-edge-colorable. Equivalently, assuming $\chi_{\text{odd}}'(G)=4$, there exists an odd $4$-edge-coloring in which color $4$ is used only once. The paper states that this conjecture is resolved by its results; it is the edge analogue of the vertex-deletion part of the odd edge-coloring theory.
363540.source_name: Xiao-Chuan Liu, Mirko Petruševski and Xu Yang, “On Graph Odd Edge-Colorings and Odd Edge-Coverings”, arXiv:2406.10192 (2025).
363540.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10192

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

363595.title: Spectral supersaturation-stability conjecture for bipartiteness
363595.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $t>0$, and let $t(G)$ denote the number of triangles. A graph is **$t$-far from being bipartite** if at least $t$ edges must be removed to make it bipartite; let $\lambda(G)$ denote its spectral radius and let $T_{n,2}$ be the balanced complete bipartite Turán graph. **Spectral supersaturation-stability conjecture.** If $G$ is $t$-far from being bipartite, then

$$
t(G)\ge\frac{n}{6}\bigl(\lambda(G)+t-\lambda(T_{n,2})\bigr).
$$
 The conjecture is proposed as a spectral analogue of a proved edge-based supersaturation-stability theorem and would imply the stated problem of Zhai and Lin.
363595.source_name: Yongtao Li, Lihua Feng and Yuejian Peng, “A spectral Erdős-Faudree-Rousseau theorem”, arXiv:2406.13176 (2025).
363595.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13176

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363596.title: Spectral triangular-edge counting conjecture
363596.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, let $\lambda(G)$ denote its spectral radius, and let $t(G)$ denote the number of triangular edges. **Spectral triangular-edge counting conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda(G)\ge\sqrt m,
$$

then $G$ has at least $\sqrt m$ triangular edges, unless $G$ is a complete bipartite graph. This strengthens the cited result giving only $\lfloor(\sqrt m-1)/2\rfloor$ triangles under the same spectral condition; the source gives no resolution status.
363596.source_name: Yongtao Li, Lihua Feng and Yuejian Peng, “A spectral Erdős-Faudree-Rousseau theorem”, arXiv:2406.13176 (2025).
363596.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13176

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363639.title: Lando's uniqueness conjecture for the sl(2)-weight system
363639.statement:
A **4-invariant** is a graph-theoretic counterpart of a weight system on chord diagrams; the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-weight system is the weight system associated with the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$.

**Lando's conjecture.** There exists a unique 4-invariant that extends the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-weight system.

The conjecture asks whether the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-weight system has a unique extension from chord diagrams to a 4-invariant. The paper does not resolve it, but constructs an explicit 4-invariant extending the specialization at $c=\frac{3}{8}$.
363639.source_name: Daniil Fomichev and Maksim Karev, “The sl(2)-weight system at c = 3/8 for graphs”, arXiv:2406.15084 (2025).
363639.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15084

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2024). “While we do not resolve the Lando conjecture, we present an explicit construction of a 4-invariant extending the specialization of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-weight system at $c = \frac 38$.”

363734.title: The conjectured sharp lower bound for observability constants on high-dimensional tori
363734.statement:
Let $m_d(r)$ be the optimal observability constant for Laplacian eigenfunctions on the $d$-dimensional torus observed on a ball of radius $r$. For $d\geq 4$, let $C_d$ and $C'_d$ be the constants appearing in the conjectured matching lower and upper bounds. **Sharp observability-bound conjecture.** If $d\geq 4$, then

$$
\exp\bigl\{-C_d r^{3-d}\bigr\} \lesssim m_d(r) \lesssim \exp\bigl\{-C'_d r^{3-d} \bigr\}.
$$

This conjecture says that the optimal lower bound for $m_d(r)$ matches the upper bound obtained in the paper. The source reports strong evidence for the conjectures in this section, but gives no resolution of this claim.
363734.source_name: Pierre Germain, Iván Moyano and Hui Zhu, “On the vanishing of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on tori”, arXiv:2406.19925 (2025).
363734.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19925

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

363774.title: The symmetric theta conjecture for decorated trees
363774.statement:
Let $\beta$ be a weak composition, let $\mathsf{RTT}_0(\beta)=\bigcup_{\alpha\vDash_0\lvert\beta\rvert}\mathsf{RTT}_0(\alpha,\beta)$, and let $\operatorname{oldXi}$ be the symmetric-function operator defined in the paper. Write $\mathsf{inv}(T)$ and $\alpha(T)$ for the inversion statistic and associated composition of $T$. **The symmetric theta conjecture.**

$$
\left.\operatorname{oldXi}e_\beta\right\rvert_{t=1}=\sum_{T\in\mathsf{RTT}_0(\beta)}q^{\mathsf{inv}(T)}x^{\alpha(T)}.
$$

This is the $q$-enumerative tree formula conjectured in the cited work and is presented here as a conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
363774.source_name: Alessandra Caraceni and Alessandro Iraci, “A Proof of the Symmetric Theta Conjecture when q = 0”, arXiv:2407.02368 (2024).
363774.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02368

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

363906.title: The diagonal recurrence conjecture for Betti numbers of squared-path cut complexes
363906.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, let $P_n^2$ denote its square, and let $\beta_k(k+r)$ be the unique nonzero Betti number of the $(r-1)$-dimensional shellable cut complex $4\Delta_k(P_{k+r}^2)4$ for the squared path, where $r\ge 3$. 

**Diagonal recurrence conjecture.** For each fixed $r\ge 3$ and $k\ge r+3$, these numbers satisfy

$$
\beta(k,k+r)=\binom{r}{1}\beta(k-1,k-1+r)-\binom{r}{2}\beta(k-2,k-2+r)+\cdots+(-1)^{r-1}\binom{r}{r}\beta(k-r,k-r+r).
$$

The known values are $\beta(3,n)=\binom{n-4}{2}$, $\beta(k,k+2)=0$, and $\beta(k,k+3)=\binom{k-1}{2}$ for $k\ge 3$. The first diagonal is already accounted for, while subsequent diagonals agree with identified integer sequences; the recurrence remains conjectural in general.
363906.source_name: Margaret Bayer, Mark Denker, Marija Jelić Milutinović, Sheila Sundaram and Lei Xue, “Topology of Cut Complexes II”, arXiv:2407.08158 (2024).
363906.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

364125.title: Cohomological spectral-sequence conjecture for locally analytic vectors
364125.statement:
Let $G$ be a compact $p$-adic Lie group, let $M$ be a $G$-module in the setting of the paper, and let $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{la}}^j(M)$ denote the $j$th derived functor of locally analytic vectors. **Spectral-sequence conjecture.** There exists a spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{i,j}=\mathrm{H}^i\bigl(G,\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{la}}^j(M)\bigr)\Rightarrow \mathrm{H}^{i+j}(G,M).
$$

This would relate group cohomology of the derived locally analytic-vector functors to the cohomology of $M$ and is presented as an analogy with a result cited in the paper.
364125.source_name: Gal Porat, “Locally analytic vectors and decompletion in mixed characteristic”, arXiv:2407.19791 (2025).
364125.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19791

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

364139.title: The equitable semialgebraic regularity conjecture
364139.statement:
Let $H$ be a $k$-partite semialgebraic hypergraph in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with total degree $D$, and let $\varepsilon>0$. An **equitable partition** is a partition of each vertex part into parts of equal size, with the regularity properties asserted by the equitable semialgebraic regularity lemma.

**Equitable regularity conjecture.** The equitable semialgebraic regularity lemma holds with partitions into

$$
O_{d,k}\left((D/\varepsilon)^d\right)
$$

parts.

The proved regularity lemma has a loss in the dependence on $\varepsilon$ when passing to equitable partitions. The conjecture asks whether that loss can be removed in every dimension; the source notes that this is possible by a direct argument in dimension $d=1$.
364139.source_name: Jonathan Tidor and Hung-Hsun Hans Yu, “Multilevel polynomial partitioning and semialgebraic hypergraphs: regularity, Turán, and Zarankiewicz results”, arXiv:2407.20221 (2024).
364139.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.20221

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).
